Scenarios.Scenario: Normal editor assertions during text-edit construction, diff computation, inline completions, and observable update completion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The assertion predicate executes synchronously on the editor/reactive-model path; because it succeeds, the modified failure branch is not entered, so progress is unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Invocation count scales with edits, diff alignments, ghost-text construction, and observable update completions, but every successful invocation performs exactly the same single predicate evaluation before and after the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in the invoking editor or model update; the diff does not add queues, parallelism, serialization, or contention.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read, populated, invalidated, or bypassed by this change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the sole hunk deletes two lines inside the falsy branch after the first predicate evaluation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Caller frequency varies by editing activity and document size, but the changed code is unreachable on successful assertions, eliminating magnitude uncertainty for the normal path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: normal hot paths execute identically before and after the change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Failed assertFn invariant while running editor or reactive-model code
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After a predicate fails, the function synchronously reevaluates it and reports BugIndicatingError; the diff removes the intervening debugger pause, shortening rather than lengthening this exceptional path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the number of invariant failures, but the PR removes one debugger statement per failure and leaves the existing second predicate evaluation and error reporting unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous failure handler invocation; no new concurrency, batching, or backpressure behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete diff only deletes the debugger statement and its lint suppression, with no added work or retained state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether developer tools are attached determines whether the removed statement paused execution; this affects the size of the improvement, not the absence of a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the exceptional path removes a potential synchronous execution pause and introduces no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, serialization, allocation, or lifecycle cost.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and representative callers in editor diffing, text edits, inline completions, merge editor, and observable updates. The change only removes a debugger pause from assertFn's failure branch; successful paths are unchanged and failed paths do less synchronous work. No performance finding or sufficiently evidenced shipped-regression record applies.
